cards.subject: math

objective.text: See that each place value unit is 10 times the unit to its right. Write it as an equation.

explanations.title: 10 times as much
explanations.text: 10 ones make 1 ten. We say 1 ten is 10 times as much as 1 one.

explanations.title: The pattern of tens
explanations.text: 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand. Each unit is 10 times as much as the unit to its right.

explanations.title: Write it as an equation
explanations.text: Show 10 times as many with an equation. For example, 10 × 2 ones = 20 ones = 2 tens.

explanations.title: Ways to model 10 times as many
explanations.text: You can model it with money, blocks, disks, drawings, dots or a tape diagram.

examples.title: 10 times 2 ones
examples.text: 10 × 2 ones = 20 ones = 2 tens. Bundle 10 ones into 1 ten, twice.

examples.title: 10 times 4 tens
examples.text: 10 × 4 tens = 40 tens = 4 hundreds.

examples.title: 10 times 7 hundreds
examples.text: 10 × 7 hundreds = 70 hundreds = 7 thousands.

examples.title: 10 times 9 hundreds
examples.text: 10 × 9 hundreds = 90 hundreds = 9 thousands. This skips the extra step.

hints.text: Think of the multiplication fact with the same numbers.
Bundle the smaller units into one larger unit. Count how many you bundle.
Say the number with its unit. For example, say 3 ones, then bundle.
Compare a unit to the unit on its right. How many copies fit?
Undo the times. Use division.
Multiply the number by 10. Think of 10 copies.
Add the four sides. Or add the length and width and double it.
Multiply the length by the width.
Say each digit with its unit, like 2 thousands 3 hundreds.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: See that a digit is worth 10 times the same digit one place right. Multiply and divide by 10.

explanations.title: Build the chart to 1 million
explanations.text: 10 hundreds make 1 thousand. 10 thousands make 1 ten thousand. 10 ten thousands make 1 hundred thousand. 10 hundred thousands make 1 million.

explanations.title: Bundle and move left
explanations.text: When you have 10 of one unit, bundle them. Move the bundle to the next column on the left.

explanations.title: Multiply many copies by 10
explanations.text: 10 × 4 ten thousands = 40 ten thousands = 4 hundred thousands. The unit gets 10 times as big.

explanations.title: Divide by unbundling
explanations.text: To divide 2 thousands by 10, unbundle each thousand into 10 hundreds. 20 hundreds ÷ 10 = 2 hundreds.

explanations.title: Two units at once
explanations.text: Put two units in parentheses to show one number. Multiply or divide both units by 10.

examples.title: 10 times 3 hundreds 2 tens
examples.text: 10 × (3 hundreds 2 tens) = 3 thousands 2 hundreds = 3,200.

examples.title: 4 ten thousands 2 tens divided by 10
examples.text: (4 ten thousands 2 tens) ÷ 10 = 4 thousands 2 ones = 4,002.

examples.title: 2 thousands divided by 10
examples.text: 2 thousands ÷ 10 = 20 hundreds ÷ 10 = 2 hundreds.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Name numbers within 1 million. Use the place value chart and commas to group units.

explanations.title: Pattern of base ten units
explanations.text: Place values repeat in groups of three: ones, tens, hundreds. Then thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. Then millions, ten millions, hundred millions.

explanations.title: Naming bigger units
explanations.text: 10 hundred millions is renamed 1 billion. The next units are ten billions and hundred billions.

explanations.title: Commas group units by three
explanations.text: A comma marks each group of 3 digits. For example, ten billion is written 10,000,000,000.

explanations.title: Read a number by its groups
explanations.text: Read the number in each group. Then say the unit name of the group. 430,325 is read four hundred thirty thousand, three hundred twenty-five.

explanations.title: Bundle to the largest unit
explanations.text: Bundle 10 of one unit into 1 of the next larger unit.

explanations.title: 10 times with two units
explanations.text: Multiply each unit by 10. 10 times 5 hundreds 3 tens is 5 thousands 3 hundreds, or 5,300.

objective.text: Read and write numbers with digits, number words and expanded form.

explanations.title: Expanded form
explanations.text: Expanded form shows the value of each digit in an addition sentence. 1,708 is 1,000 plus 700 plus 8.

explanations.title: A zero adds nothing
explanations.text: A zero has no term in expanded form. Zero added to a number does not change its value.

explanations.title: Word form and commas
explanations.text: Say what you read, and write it in words. The comma separates the thousands from the hundreds, tens and ones.

explanations.text: Write each part you hear. Then put the number in the place value chart and in expanded form.

explanations.title: Expanded form to standard form
explanations.text: Place each term in its place value. Then write the sum as digits.

hints.text: Count by fours. Get to the next ten first, then count on.
Say the unit form. Then write each digit in its place.
Multiply the number by the base unit. Then write it in standard form.
Add using the unit names, not the whole numbers.
Say the digit and its place. Then say its value.
Write the value of each digit with a plus sign between. Skip any zero.
Read the number by its groups. Write each group in words. Check commas and hyphens.
Write each part you hear in its place. Use a zero where no part is said.
Check the place of each digit. Compare the value of each digit with the term.
Fill the row from the form you are given. Then write the other two forms.
Think of 4,400 as hundreds. Then think of it as thousands and hundreds.

misconceptions.response_text: Check the value of the 7. In 700,000 it is 700,000, not 70,000. Use zero to hold a place.

objective.text: Compare numbers by the value of their digits. Order numbers from least to greatest.

explanations.title: Compare the largest unit first
explanations.text: Find the largest unit in both numbers. The number with more of that unit is greater.

explanations.title: If the largest units are equal
explanations.text: If the digits of the largest unit are equal, compare the next place right.

explanations.title: Comparison symbols
explanations.text: Greater than is >. Less than is <. Equal to is =. Say a comparison in two ways.

explanations.title: Order several numbers
explanations.text: Write the numbers in the place value chart. Find the first place where they differ. Then order them.

explanations.title: Numbers in different forms
explanations.text: Write the first number in standard form. Then compare place by place.

examples.title: 3,010 and 2,040
examples.text: Thousands is the largest unit. 3 thousands is greater than 2 thousands, so 3,010 > 2,040.

examples.title: 43,021 and 45,302
examples.text: Both have 4 ten thousands. 3 thousands is less than 5 thousands, so 43,021 < 45,302.

examples.title: Three numbers in order
examples.text: 32,644 > 32,534 > 32,434. All three have 3 ten thousands and 2 thousands. The hundreds differ.

examples.title: 700,000 + 30,000 + 20 + 8 and 735,008
examples.text: The first number is 730,028. 730,028 < 735,008 because 0 thousands is less than 5 thousands.

objective.text: Find 1, 10 and 100 thousand more and less than a number.

explanations.title: 1 thousand more or less
explanations.text: To find 1 thousand more, add 1 to the thousands digit. To find 1 thousand less, take 1 from it. The other digits stay the same.

explanations.title: 10 thousand more or less
explanations.text: 10 thousand is 1 ten thousand. Change the ten thousands digit by 1. The other digits stay the same.

explanations.title: 100 thousand more or less
explanations.text: 100 thousand is 1 hundred thousand. Change the hundred thousands digit by 1. The other digits stay the same.

explanations.title: Patterns in place value
explanations.text: In a pattern like 545,000, 445,000, 345,000 only one unit changes. Here the hundred thousands decrease by 1 each time.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Round numbers to the nearest thousand using a vertical number line.

explanations.title: Find the two thousands
explanations.text: To round to the nearest thousand, find the thousand below the number. Then find the thousand above it. These are the endpoints.

explanations.title: Halfway point
explanations.text: The halfway point is 500 more than the lower thousand. 4,500 is halfway between 4,000 and 5,000.

explanations.title: Nearer endpoint
explanations.text: If a number is below the halfway point, it rounds down. If it is above the halfway point, it rounds up.

explanations.title: Halfway rounds up
explanations.text: If a number is exactly halfway, we round up. 14,500 rounded to the nearest thousand is 15,000.

explanations.title: Thousands in a number
explanations.text: Say how many thousands are in the number. One more thousand gives the upper endpoint.

examples.title: Round 4,100 and 4,700
examples.text: 4,100 is nearer to 4,000, so it rounds to 4,000. 4,700 is nearer to 5,000, so it rounds to 5,000.

examples.title: Midpoint of 31,000 and 32,000
examples.text: 31,000 is 310 hundreds and 32,000 is 320 hundreds. The midpoint is 315 hundreds, or 31,500.

objective.text: Round numbers to any place using a vertical number line. Estimate sums and differences.

explanations.title: Round to the nearest ten thousand
explanations.text: Find the ten thousand below and the ten thousand above. The halfway point is 5 thousands more than the lower one.

explanations.title: Round to the nearest hundred thousand
explanations.text: Find the hundred thousand below and above. The halfway point is 5 ten thousands more than the lower one.

explanations.title: Nearer endpoint
explanations.text: Mark the number on the line. It rounds to the endpoint it is nearer to. At the halfway point, round up.

explanations.title: Estimate a sum
explanations.text: Round each addend to the same place. Then add the rounded numbers.

explanations.title: Estimate a difference
explanations.text: Round each number to the same place. Then subtract. Rounding to a smaller unit gives an estimate closer to the actual answer.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Round numbers to any place to make good estimates in real world problems.

explanations.title: Smaller units are closer
explanations.text: Rounding to the largest unit gives the most zeros and the easiest number. Rounding to a smaller unit gives an estimate closer to the actual number.

explanations.title: Choose the best estimate
explanations.text: Look at the situation. Use patterns or data to decide which unit to round to.

explanations.title: Enough for everyone
explanations.text: If everyone needs one, it is better to have more than not enough. Sometimes you round up even if the digits say round down.

explanations.title: The largest unit can mislead
explanations.text: Rounding to the largest unit can give a number below or above the actual number. Choose the unit that fits the situation.

explanations.title: Multiply tens by tens
explanations.text: 3 tens times 4 tens is 12 hundreds, not 12 tens.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Add multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm. Solve word problems with tape diagrams.

explanations.title: Standard addition algorithm
explanations.text: Write the numbers one above the other with the places lined up. Add the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds, and so on, moving left.

explanations.title: Regroup 10 of a unit
explanations.text: Bundle 10 of one unit as 1 of the next larger unit. Write the 1 in the next column.

explanations.title: One digit in each column
explanations.text: Do not write two digits in one column. 13 tens is 1 hundred and 3 tens.

explanations.title: Tape diagram
explanations.text: A tape diagram shows the parts and the whole. A bracket marks the whole. A letter stands for the unknown number.

explanations.title: Variable
explanations.text: When a letter stands for an unknown number, we call the letter a variable.

explanations.title: Answer statement
explanations.text: Write a sentence that tells the answer. Use the words and the context of the problem.

explanations.title: Multiply tens by tens
explanations.text: 3 tens times 4 tens is 12 hundreds, not 12 tens.

examples.title: 3,134 plus 2,493
examples.text: 4 ones plus 3 ones is 7 ones. 3 tens plus 9 tens is 12 tens, so bundle 10 tens as 1 hundred. 1 hundred plus 4 hundreds plus 1 hundred is 6 hundreds. 3 thousands plus 2 thousands is 5 thousands. The sum is 5,627.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Solve multi-step addition word problems with tape diagrams. Check answers by rounding.

explanations.title: Tape for each quantity
explanations.text: Draw one tape for each quantity. If one quantity is more than another, extend its tape by the extra amount.

explanations.title: Multi-step problems
explanations.text: Find the missing quantity first. Then find the total. Use a letter for the unknown.

explanations.title: Estimate first
explanations.text: Before you solve, round each number to get a general sense of the answer. After you solve, compare the answer with the estimate.

explanations.title: Reasonable answers
explanations.text: An answer is reasonable if it is close to the estimate. If it is not close, check your work.

explanations.title: Smaller units are closer
explanations.text: Rounding to a smaller unit gives an estimate closer to the actual answer. Rounding to a larger unit has a larger margin of error.

objective.text: Subtract multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm, regrouping once. Solve word problems with tape diagrams.

explanations.title: Are we ready to subtract?
explanations.text: Look across the top number from right to left. Check that each column has enough units to subtract the bottom number.

explanations.title: Unbundle a larger unit
explanations.text: If a column lacks units, unbundle 1 unit from the column on the left. It becomes 10 of this unit. Rename both numbers.

explanations.title: Subtract and name units
explanations.text: When every column is ready, subtract from right to left. Name the units as you go.

explanations.title: Check by adding
explanations.text: To check a subtraction, add the difference to the part you subtracted. The sum should be the whole.

explanations.title: Tape diagram for subtraction
explanations.text: The whole is the long tape. The known part and the unknown part are under it. A letter marks the unknown part.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Subtract with the standard algorithm, regrouping up to three times. Solve word problems with tape diagrams.

explanations.title: Regroup twice
explanations.text: Check each column from right to left. Every column that lacks units needs 1 unit unbundled from the column on its left.

explanations.title: Zero in the unbundling column
explanations.text: If the next column on the left has none, look one more column left. Unbundle there, then pass the units down.

explanations.title: Start in any ready column
explanations.text: After the top number is ready, you can subtract in any column. Name the units as you subtract.

explanations.title: Check by adding
explanations.text: Add the difference to the part you subtracted. The sum should be the whole.

explanations.title: Choose a variable
explanations.text: A letter stands for the unknown number in the tape diagram. The letter can match the thing you find.

objective.text: Subtract with the standard algorithm, regrouping many times, even through zeros. Solve word problems.

explanations.title: Regroup many times
explanations.text: Check every column from right to left. Each column that lacks units needs 1 unit unbundled from its left. You may regroup in many columns.

explanations.title: Regroup through zeros
explanations.text: If a number has zeros, unbundle the first non-zero unit on the left. Pass units down through each zero.

explanations.title: Subtract from 1,000,000
explanations.text: Rename 1,000,000 as 9s in every place and 10 ones. Then every column is ready to subtract.

explanations.title: Check by adding the parts
explanations.text: Add the difference to the part you subtracted. The sum should be the whole.

explanations.title: Tape diagram shows the operation
explanations.text: The tape shows the whole and the parts. If you know the whole and one part, subtract to find the other part.

objective.text: Solve two-step subtraction word problems with tape diagrams. Check answers by rounding.

explanations.title: Two-step problems
explanations.text: Find what is missing first, or find the total of the parts you know. Then use that to find the answer.

explanations.title: Estimate, then solve
explanations.text: Round the numbers first to get a general sense of the answer. Then find the exact answer and compare.

explanations.title: Reasonable answers
explanations.text: An answer is reasonable if it is near the estimate. Rounding the exact answer to the same place should match the estimate.

explanations.title: Compare with a smaller unknown
explanations.text: If one amount is fewer than another, subtract to find it. Then use both amounts to find the total.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Solve additive compare word problems with tape diagrams. Find how much more or fewer.

explanations.title: What compare means
explanations.text: To compare, put two amounts side by side. The difference tells how much more or fewer one is.

explanations.title: How much more
explanations.text: Draw two tapes, one for each amount. The unknown is the missing part, the difference. So subtract the smaller from the larger.

explanations.title: Fewer and less
explanations.text: Say fewer when talking about separate things, like apples. Say less for amounts like juice.

explanations.title: Two-step compare
explanations.text: Sometimes you find one amount first. Then draw a new double tape to compare the two amounts.

explanations.title: Three-step compare
explanations.text: Find each amount at first. Use the relationship in the story, like double. Then compare.

cards.subject: math

objective.text: Solve multi-step word problems with tape diagrams. Check answers by rounding.

explanations.title: Multi-step problems
explanations.text: Find each missing amount one step at a time. Then add or subtract to find what the question asks.

explanations.title: More than one way
explanations.text: You can find each amount and add. Or you can add like units first. Both ways are right.

explanations.title: Check with the diagram
explanations.text: Look at the tape diagram. Round each amount and add the rounded amounts. Your exact answer should be close.

explanations.title: Count in thousands
explanations.text: 2 thousand more and 2 thousand fewer cancel out. Those two weeks add up to 2 times week 1.

hints.text: Rename the larger unit as smaller units. Then subtract.
Think how many more it takes to reach the next unit.
Think how many centimeters make one meter.
Find the total and the parts you know. Subtract the parts from the total.
Subtract the known parts from the total.
Think about what the tape diagram shows about the parts and the total.

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses tape diagrams the child draws and the source diagrams are pictures. The child cannot draw here.
assets_required.description: A tape diagram builder. The child types an equation with a variable and sees a tape diagram with the parts, the total bracket and the unknown. The child can then solve for the variable.
must_show_exactly: A text box for an equation with a variable
A tape diagram with one segment for each part
A bracket for the total
A highlighted segment for the unknown
A box to type the value of the variable
An estimate check next to the exact answer
states_or_frames: Tape diagram drawn from the equation
assets_required.interaction: Child types an equation. The widget draws the tape. The child solves for the variable and checks it with an estimate.
assets_required.alt_text: A tape diagram drawn from an equation with the unknown highlighted.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean tape diagram with three labeled segments, a bracket for the total and one highlighted unknown with a variable. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source tape diagrams are pictures with no numbers in the .md. Build from typed equations.

q_db_1 to q_db_4 accept any clear answer that fits. A person should check how they are marked.

The source states no misconception for this lesson. A possible one is writing a story that does not match the total and the parts in the diagram. Do not use it until a person confirms.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
